items.followUp: Why do crystalline solids have a definite melting point?

rubric.why: Amorphous solids lack the regular, orderly arrangement of particles found in crystals.
rubric.description: States that the particles are arranged irregularly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the irregular arrangement of particles in an amorphous solid.

rubric.why: Different parts of an amorphous solid soften or melt at different temperatures, rather than at one fixed temperature.
rubric.description: Explains that amorphous solids soften over a range of temperatures.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that they soften or melt over a temperature range rather than at a sharp melting point.

modelAnswer: Amorphous solids have an irregular arrangement of particles.
Different parts soften gradually over a range of temperatures, so they do not have a sharp melting point.

items.followUp: Define solubility and name a solvent commonly used to dissolve paint.

rubric.why: Solubility is defined by the greatest amount of solute that can dissolve to make a saturated solution.
rubric.description: Defines solubility as the maximum amount of solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a stated temperature to form a saturated solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the maximum amount and saturated-solution idea; the stated temperature or fixed amount of solvent may be implicit.

rubric.why: Turpentine is a solvent used to dissolve many paints.
rubric.description: Names turpentine oil as a solvent for paints.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for turpentine or turpentine oil.

modelAnswer: Solubility is the maximum amount of a solute that dissolves in a given amount of solvent at a particular temperature to form a saturated solution.
Paints are soluble in turpentine oil.

items.followUp: What is a suspension? Give one example.

rubric.why: A suspension contains undissolved particles dispersed in another substance.
rubric.description: Defines a suspension as a heterogeneous mixture in which insoluble solid particles are dispersed in a liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying a mixture of dispersed, insoluble particles; settling may be included.

rubric.why: Muddy water and chalk in water are common examples of suspensions.
rubric.description: Gives a suitable example of a suspension.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct example such as muddy water or chalk in water.

modelAnswer: A suspension is a heterogeneous mixture in which insoluble solid particles are dispersed in a liquid and may settle on standing.
Muddy water is an example of a suspension.

items.followUp: Describe how water molecules interact with the ions when sodium chloride dissolves in water.

rubric.why: Dissolving sodium chloride separates it into sodium and chloride ions.
rubric.description: States that sodium chloride separates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both ions formed from NaCl.

rubric.why: Water molecules interact with and surround the ions, forming hydrated ions.
rubric.description: States that water molecules attract and hydrate or surround the ions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing hydration or the surrounding of the ions by water molecules.

modelAnswer: Sodium chloride separates into Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions in water.
Water molecules attract and surround these ions, forming hydrated ions.

rubric.why: Zinc, iron, lead and tin are examples of moderately reactive metals.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct example.

rubric.why: The question asks for any two metals from the moderately reactive group.
rubric.description: Names a second, different moderately reactive metal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second correct example.

modelAnswer: Zinc is a moderately reactive metal.
Iron is another moderately reactive metal.

items.followUp: Write two physical properties of copper.

rubric.why: Silver is lustrous and is also malleable, ductile, or a good conductor of heat and electricity.
rubric.description: Gives one correct characteristic of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one characteristic such as lustre, malleability, ductility, or good conductivity.

rubric.why: Any two distinct correct characteristics satisfy the question.
rubric.description: Gives a second correct characteristic of silver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a second distinct characteristic.

modelAnswer: It is also malleable and a good conductor of heat and electricity.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for the reaction of methane with chlorine in sunlight.

rubric.why: The reaction is the substitution of one hydrogen atom in methane by chlorine.
rubric.description: Gives the correct reactants and products in the balanced equation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for CH₄ + Cl₂ → CH₃Cl + HCl, with or without state symbols.

rubric.why: Bright sunlight initiates the substitution reaction between methane and chlorine.
rubric.description: Identifies the sunlight condition or the reaction as substitution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for indicating bright sunlight or naming the reaction as substitution.

modelAnswer: The reaction takes place in bright sunlight and is a substitution reaction.

items.followUp: How does the ozone layer help protect living organisms?

rubric.why: Ozone in the atmosphere absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
rubric.description: Identifies ozone and its absorption of ultraviolet radiation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that ozone absorbs or blocks harmful UV radiation.

rubric.why: By absorbing UV radiation, ozone helps protect living things from its harmful effects.
rubric.description: Explains that this protection benefits living organisms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the blocked UV radiation to protection of life.

modelAnswer: Ozone, an allotrope of oxygen, absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the Sun.
This protects living organisms from the harmful effects of that radiation.
